long_names = set()

for _, row in matches.iterrows():
    df_event, _, _, _ = parser.event(row["match_id"])
    
    for col in ["player_name", "pass_recipient_name"]:
        names = df_event[col].dropna()
        names = names[names.str.split().str.len() > 3].unique()
        long_names.update(names)

text:
1. Pass Map Viz - Buildup to the Shot


Code
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 8))
fig.patch.set_facecolor('#ffffff')
fig.suptitle('Pass Buildup to Shot (Within 15 Seconds)',
             color='black', fontsize=22, y=1.04, fontweight = 'bold')

for ax, passes_df, team, color in zip(
    axes,
    [arg_pre_shot, ksa_pre_shot],
    ["Argentina", "Saudi Arabia"],
    ['#75AADB', '#00b100']
):
    pitch = Pitch(
        pitch_type='statsbomb',
        pitch_color='#fafafa',
        line_color='#cccccc',
        line_zorder=2
    )
    pitch.draw(ax=ax)

    # complete passes
    complete = passes_df[passes_df['outcome_name'].isna()]
    if not complete.empty:
        pitch.arrows(
            complete.x, complete.y,
            complete.end_x, complete.end_y,
            ax=ax,
            color=color,
            width=2,
            headwidth=4,
            alpha=0.8,
            label='Complete'
        )

    # incomplete passes
    incomplete = passes_df[passes_df['outcome_name'].notna()]
    if not incomplete.empty:
        pitch.arrows(
            incomplete.x, incomplete.y,
            incomplete.end_x, incomplete.end_y,
            ax=ax,
            color='#000000',
            width=1.5,
            headwidth=3,
            alpha=0.9,
            label='Incomplete'
        )

    ax.set_title(team, color='black', fontsize=13, pad=10)
    ax.legend(facecolor='#fafafa', labelcolor='black',
              loc='upper left', fontsize=13,
              markerscale=1.5,
              framealpha=0.8
              )

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('images/pass_map.png', dpi=150,
            bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='#fafafa')
plt.show()









Why Track passes 15 seconds before a shot?
This type of tracking reveals the precise off ball movements, spacing and defensive fractures that create scoring opportunities, rather than just analyzing the final action. If the coach only looks at shots, then they’re reacting only to the outcome. Looking at passes 15 seconds before a shot can give an idea of spatial patterns before looking at the shot map
🟦 Argentina Takeaways

The high volume of passes show that Argentina dominated possession
Short and quick arrows are clustered together meaning a lot of tight passing was carried out
Argentina controlled the ball and recycled possession heavily in the opponent’s half creating a sustained attacking pressure

🟩 Saudi Takeways
Saudi Arabia sat deeper, played fewer passes and relied on direct balls when they played forward

def draw_passing_network(ax, passes_df, team, color, top5):
    """Passing network for top 5 players"""
    
    # passes between top 5 players only
    complete = passes_df[
        passes_df['outcome_name'].isna() &
        passes_df['pass_recipient_name'].notna() &
        passes_df['player_name'].isin(top5) &
        passes_df['pass_recipient_name'].isin(top5)
    ]

    # pass pairs
    pairs = complete.groupby(
        ['player_name', 'pass_recipient_name']
    ).size().reset_index(name='pass_count')

    # average positions
    avg_pos = complete.groupby('player_name').agg(
        avg_x=('x', 'mean'),
        avg_y=('y', 'mean'),
        total=('x', 'count')
    ).reset_index()

    pitch = Pitch(
        pitch_type='statsbomb',
        pitch_color='#fafafa',
        line_color='#cccccc'
    )
    pitch.draw(ax=ax)

    # draw lines
    for _, row in pairs.iterrows():
        p1 = avg_pos[avg_pos['player_name'] == row['player_name']]
        p2 = avg_pos[avg_pos['player_name'] == row['pass_recipient_name']]
        if not p1.empty and not p2.empty:
            pitch.lines(
                p1.avg_x.values[0], p1.avg_y.values[0],
                p2.avg_x.values[0], p2.avg_y.values[0],
                ax=ax,
                lw=row['pass_count'] * 0.4,
                color=color,
                alpha=0.5,
                zorder=1
            )

    # draw nodes
    pitch.scatter(
        avg_pos.avg_x, avg_pos.avg_y,
        s=avg_pos.total * 8,
        c=color,
        edgecolors='white',
        linewidth=1,
        ax=ax,
        zorder=3
    )

    # last name only
    texts = []
    for _, row in avg_pos.iterrows():
        last_name = row['player_name'].split()[-1]
        txt = ax.text(
            row['avg_x'], row['avg_y'],
            last_name,
            color='black',
            fontsize=10,
            fontweight='bold',
            ha='center',
            va='bottom',
            zorder=5
        )
        texts.append(txt)

    # adjustText: avoids label overlap
    # similar to ggrepel 
    adjust_text(
        texts,
        ax=ax,
        expand=(1.2, 1.4),
        arrowprops=dict(
            arrowstyle='-',
            color='#999999',
            lw=0.5
        )
    )

    ax.set_title(team, color='black',
                 fontsize=12, pad=12)
    return ax


# top 5 player lists
arg_top5_list = arg_top5['player_name'].tolist()
ksa_top5_list = ksa_top5['player_name'].tolist()

             color='black', fontsize=22,

fig.text(
    0.5, 1.00,
    'Node size = total passes \n Line width = pass frequency',
    color='#666666', fontsize=10,
    fontstyle='italic', ha='center', va='top'
)

for ax, passes_df, team, color, top5 in zip(
    axes,
    [arg_passes, ksa_passes],
    ["Argentina", "Saudi Arabia"],
    ['#75AADB', '#00b100'],
    [arg_top5_list, ksa_top5_list]

plt.tight_layout()

            bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='#fafafa')

Argentina’s top 5 passers were almost entirely confined to their own defensive third, a striking visual that tells the story of Saudi Arabia’s relentless high press. Otamendi and Romero, both center backs, were forced into heavy ball circulation at the back, with Paredes and De Paul dropping deep to offer passing options rather than driving forward. The tightly clustered network suggests Argentina struggled to progress the ball through midfield and build attacks from deep (an unusual sight for a team of their quality)
Saudi Arabia’s network tells the opposite story. Their top 5 passers operated across a wider area of the pitch, with Owais distributing from deep while Al-Malki, Kanoo and Hamid formed an active midfield triangle in the center of the pitch

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(14, 10))  
fig.patch.set_facecolor('#fafafa')
fig.suptitle('Touch Heatmaps',
             color='black', fontsize=16,
             fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
fig.text(
    0.5, 0.99,
    'Based on pass locations across the full match',
    color='#666666', fontsize=10,
    fontstyle='italic', ha='center',  va='top'
)

for ax, passes_df, team, cmap in zip(
    axes,
    [arg_passes, ksa_passes],
    ["Argentina", "Saudi Arabia"],
    ['Blues', 'Greens']
):
    pitch = Pitch(
        pitch_type='statsbomb',
        pitch_color='#fafafa',
        line_color='#cccccc'
    )
    

    pitch.kdeplot(
        passes_df.x, passes_df.y,
        ax=ax,
        cmap=cmap,
        fill=True,
        alpha=0.3,
        levels=10,       
        thresh=0.16,     
        bw_adjust=1.2
    )

    pitch.draw(ax=ax)
    
    ax.set_title(team, color='black',
                 fontsize=13, pad=12)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('images/heatmap.png', dpi=150,
            bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='#fafafa')
plt.show()









Argentina’s right sided concentration reflects both their natural build up structure through De Paul and Paredes and Saudi Arabia’s success in forcing Argentina to recycle possession sideways in their own half, rather than progress forward.
Saudi Arabia’s touches were spread across a much wider central zone, with two distinct hotspots - 1. Deep right where they absorbed Argentine pressure 2. In the central midfield where they launched their counter attacks.
The coverage across the full width of their defensive and middle third reflects a well defined defensive shape that utilized space effectively
